problem: RNR-Map supports image-goal navigation and rendering but cannot be queried with natural language. Language-grounded maps like VLMaps lack NeRF rendering and image-goal querying, and LERF is slow and limited to small scenes.
motivation: A single map that supports image queries, open-vocabulary text queries and rendering of the path to the goal would give users a low-effort language interface to the agent. It would also let users preview paths without physically moving the agent, which helps when a query is ambiguous.
key_idea: Concatenate frozen CLIP image features (512-d) with RNR-Map latent codes (32-d) in each map cell, then localize text queries by cosine similarity, with negative prompts, and render the path with NeRF/GSN.
insight: The paper reports that negative prompts (scene-specific background or distractor phrases) give cleaner similarity maps. Average success rises from 0.66 to 0.72 and DTS falls from 1.79 to 1.31 m, with the largest gain on Darden (success 0.37 to 0.59). The low Darden success is attributed to mesh artefacts such as mirrors and holes that corrupt the embeddings. Concatenation keeps the original RNR-Map image-goal behaviour intact while adding language search without any extra training.
method: Map creation: an RNR-Map encoder-decoder (from the original RNR-Map) yields 32-d pixel latent codes. These are projected to a 2D grid using depth and odometry from a random-walk exploration.
Language features: a pre-trained CLIP image encoder gives a 512-d feature per RGB-D frame. It is concatenated with the RNR features into a 544-d cell embedding and projected to the map.

Text query localization: the CLIP text embedding is compared by cosine similarity with every map cell. The maximum-similarity cell is the goal, lifted to a 3D pose via inverse projection with a roto-translation matrix.
Negative prompting: scene-specific unwanted or background prompts (e.g. wall, floor, stuff) are compared alongside the target prompt, following LERF/CLIP, to sharpen the similarity maps.

Path rendering and orientation: an extension of GSN synthesizes views along a shortest path. Near the goal, the agent rotates 360° to pick the heading with maximal CLIP similarity. MaskCLIP pixel-wise features give saliency of the goal.

Ambiguity and multi-object search: after the max, neighbouring cells are suppressed and the search repeats for peaks above a 0.6 threshold, rendering a path for each. Multiple targets are searched sequentially.
Affordance search: GPT-3.5 turns an indirect query into a list of target descriptions (e.g. rooms), which are then searched sequentially.

setting.backbone: RNR-Map encoder-decoder (pre-trained) + CLIP (frozen) + GSN + MaskCLIP; GPT-3.5-turbo for affordance queries
setting.training_data: none for the new components (off-the-shelf CLIP; RNR-Map used as pretrained)
setting.action_space: map-based goal localization with shortest-path planning and NeRF-rendered path; no low-level policy evaluated
setting.privileged: map built beforehand by random exploration (known environment); scene-specific hand-chosen negative prompts; GT object label used as text prompt

numbers.eval_set_note: 4 scenes of the Gibson tiny val split (Corozal, Darden, Markleeville, Wiconisco)
numbers.extra: known map built beforehand; scene-specific negative prompts

numbers_note: Success is printed as fractions (0.72), not percents; kept as printed. Only a small 4-scene evaluation; no comparison to baselines. Ambiguity and affordance experiments are qualitative.
results: On four Gibson-tiny val scenes, Le-RNR-Map reaches an average success of 0.72 and DTS of 1.31 m with negative prompts, versus 0.66 and 1.79 m without. It does this with no additional training. No baselines are compared, and the multi-object, ambiguity and affordance results are qualitative.
limitations: Tiny evaluation (4 scenes, no baselines), and negative prompts are hand-picked per scene
Mesh artefacts (mirrors, holes) corrupt embeddings, causing low success on Darden
Requires a pre-built map from prior exploration; ambiguity evaluation depends on hyperparameters (N paths, threshold 0.6), and no standard ObjectNav benchmark is reported
